Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

nature noun

the character a person or thing is born with

also human nature, by nature, temperament, disposition, personality, character

classical

Hor. Ep. 1.10.24: nātūram expellēs furcā, tamen ūsque recurret
Cic. Sen. 65: nōn omnis nātūra vetustāte coacēscit

nātūra, nātūrae f.

noun, first declension

nature, character: what one is born with

By nature is nātūrā, in the ablative.

Other words

  • ingenium, ingeniī n. — a person’s nature, temperament; natural talent

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Tac. Agr. 42.4: proprium hūmānī ingeniī est ōdisse quem laeserīs; Cic. Att. 6.2.2: multiplex puerī ingenium; Traupman 349: nature (of a person)

    Traupman’s word for a person’s nature. Lewis & Short call this general sense mostly poetic and post-Augustan, but Cicero uses it of a boy’s character, and it is everywhere a person’s talent.

  • indolēs, indolis f. — natural disposition, especially of the young

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 26: adulēscentibus bonā indole praeditīs; Traupman 156, 150

    Lewis & Short: an inborn or native quality; natural abilities, disposition.

  • mōrēs, mōrum m. pl. — character, ways

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Traupman 150

    One’s character as shown in conduct; indolēs is the inborn disposition.

Examples

  • nātūram expellēs furcā, tamen ūsque recurret

    you may drive nature out with a pitchfork, but she will keep coming backHor. Ep. 1.10.24

  • proprium hūmānī ingeniī est ōdisse quem laeserīs

    it is human nature to hate the one you have hurtTac. Agr. 42.4

  • est magnum illud quidem vērum tamen multiplex puerī ingenium; quō ego regendō habeō negōtī satis

    the boy has a great nature, but a complicated one, and steering it keeps me quite busy enoughCic. Att. 6.2.2

See also nature, naughty, human, kind.
